reason: This passage primarily depicts the Israelites (regular people) as unfaithful and sinful rather than favorable. While they initially promise obedience to God's covenant (saying 'כֹּל אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהוָה נַעֲשֶׂה' - all that the Lord has spoken we will do), the dominant narrative concerns their rapid moral failure. When Moses delays on Mount Sinai, they immediately turn to Aaron demanding he make them gods ('ק֣וּם עֲשֵׂה־ לָ֣נוּ אֱלֹהִ֗ים'). They create and worship the golden calf, are described as having 'שִׁחֵ֣ת' (corrupted/spoiled themselves), and commit what is repeatedly called a 'great sin' (חֲטָאָה גְדֹלָה). The text emphasizes their impatience, idolatry, and faithlessness in breaking their covenant almost immediately after establishing it.
